title: Let the activity hook run in a herded pane and write the job mailbox activity record
action: In hooks/mod.rs, narrow the BEE_HERDING_WORKER early exit: when the marker is set, the `activity` hook name passes through to its handler; every other hook name still exits 0 silently before stdin is read (per D1; herding-worker-standalone D3 stays true for them). In hooks/activity.rs, add a herded sink (per D2): when BEE_HERDING_WORKER is set AND BEE_HERDING_JOB_ID names a job, the hook writes `.bee/mailbox/<job-id>/activity.json` tmp-then-rename with the same record shape as the sessions record plus `job_id` and `round`; it does NOT write `.bee/sessions/<id>.json` or the `.activity.jsonl` sidecar for that pane. `round` is the highest N for which `brief-N.txt` exists in that mailbox directory (the orchestrator writes the brief before it delivers the pointer, so this is the current round without a second env var); 0 when no brief exists yet. Keep the state machine (working/waiting_input/blocked/idle/exited, same-tool_use_id unblock) untouched — only the sink changes. Resolve the mailbox root from the repo's .bee directory the way the sessions sink already does. Tests in activity.rs: (1) marker + job id writes activity.json with job_id and the highest brief round and leaves sessions/ empty; (2) marker without job id falls back to today's behavior; (3) mod.rs dispatch: under the marker, `activity` runs and `tools-logger` exits 0 with no output.
judge_obligation_ack: hooks/mod.rs is a guard dispatcher but the change only narrows one early-exit branch for a never-denying hook; the guards' silence under the marker is asserted by a new unit test, and the rule stays in force for every guard hook
